full_judgment:
3. The defendant Nos. 1 and 5 contested the suit by filing separate written statements. In his written statement the defendant No. 1, contended that the suit is not maintainable, undervalued, and also barred by limitation and that for various reason the plaintiff No. 2 and her husband Dr. Bazlul Haque was antagonistic to Dr. Sadek Ali and so Dr. Sadek Ali, out of his own free will and consent, on 22.12.1976 executed a deed of heba-bil-ewaz deed at Bogra in favour of the defendant No. 1 but having faced difficulty in registering the same at Bogra, Dr. Sadek Ali registered the same at Rajshahi on 19.04.1977 and then delivered the possession of the gifted land to the defendant No. 1 in lieu of  Quran, Prayer mat and Tashbih and the said deed was neither forged nor fabricated and that on 31.01.1981, the plaintiffs including Dr. Bazlul Haque as well as other sisters of defendant No. 1 executed a solenama, Ext. A. in respect of the land left by Dr. Sadek Ali and also in respect of the criminal cases instituted between them and in the said solenama the plaintiff admitted that the above deed of heba-bil-ewaz was executed by Dr. Sadek Ali in favour of defendant No. 1 and the learned Additional District Magistrate Rajshahi wrongly convicted the defendant No. 1 and the said conviction was set aside by the High Court Division in criminal Case No. 212 of 1983 which was affirmed by the Appellate Division. In his written statement the defendant No. 5 contended that the disputed heba-bil-ewaz executed by Dr. Sadek Ali in favour of defendant No. 1 was genuine and the plaintiffs and other daughter of Dr. Sadek Ali admitted the same in the solenama Ext-A. 

 5. The learned counsel for the submits that both the parties have admitted the genuiness of the said deed of heba-bil-ewaz by putting their signatures in the solename, Exhibit-A, and though in the previously instituted criminal case the defendant No. 1petitioner was convicted by the trial court but the High Court Division, in Criminal Appeal No. 212 of 1983, acquitted him as the forgery of the heba-bil-ewaz was not proved and he above decision was also affirmed by the Appellate Division of Supreme Court in Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 55, 56 and 57 of 1984 and accordingly the High Court Division was wrong in rejecting the civil revisional application summarily and further the High Court Division also failed to consider that the above deed of heba-bil-ewaz was registered on 19.04.1977 and the solenama Ext. A was made on 31.01.1981 and the suit was filed on 28.06.1983 and as such the suit is hit by the principles of waiver, acquiescence, estoppel and limitation.
